text: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Stand in the gate of the LORD's house and proclaim this word there: Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who enter these gates to worship the LORD.
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Mend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place.
Do not trust in deceptive words, chanting, "The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD!"
But if you truly mend your ways and your deeds, if you truly deal justly with one another,

versions.text: No—if you truly mend your ways and your deeds, if you truly deal justly with one another,
versions.explanation: The opening "No—" is an abrupt interjection not supported by כִּי אִם, which here functions as an adversative introducing the condition ("but if"). "But if" preserves the contrast with verse 4 while reading more smoothly aloud, since the sentence continues into verse 7.

text: if you do not oppress the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow, if you do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own ruin,
then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land I gave to your fathers, from age to age.
But look—you are trusting in deceptive words that are worth nothing.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods you have not known,
and then come and stand before me in this house that bears my name, and say, "We are safe"—only to go on doing all these detestable things?
Has this house that bears my name become a den of robbers in your eyes? I myself have seen it, declares the LORD.
Go now to my place at Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD—I spoke to you again and again, but you would not listen; I called you, but you would not answer—
therefore I will do to this house that bears my name, the house you trust in, and to the place I gave to you and your fathers, what I did to Shiloh.
I will cast you out of my presence, just as I cast out all your kinsmen, all the offspring of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray for this people; raise no cry or prayer on their behalf, and do not plead with me, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.
But is it me they are provoking? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to their own shame?

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: My anger and my fury will be poured out on this place—on man and beast, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground—and it will burn and not be quenched.
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Go ahead, pile your burnt offerings on your sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves!
For when I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them concerning burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But this is what I commanded them: Obey my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people; walk in every way I command you, so that it may go well with you.

versions.text: This is what I commanded them: Obey my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people; walk in every way I command you, so that it may go well with you.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּי אִם marks a strong contrast with the previous verse ("I did not command them about sacrifices... but this I did command"). Adding "But" makes the contrast audible when read aloud.

text: But they did not listen or pay attention. They followed their own counsels, the stubbornness of their evil hearts, and went backward instead of forward.
From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them again and again, day after day, early and late.

versions.text: From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them again and again, day after day.
versions.explanation: Minor rhythm note: "again and again, day after day" already renders יוֹם הַשְׁכֵּם וְשָׁלֹחַ twice over and sounds slightly redundant when read aloud. If the fuller idiom is wanted, a single tightened phrase is preferable; otherwise consider trimming to "sending them again and again, day after day" only once (e.g. drop "again and again").

text: Yet they did not listen to me or pay attention. They stiffened their necks and did worse than their fathers.
So you will speak all these words to them, and they will not listen to you; you will call to them, and they will not answer you.
Then say to them: This is the nation that would not obey the voice of the LORD its God or accept correction. Faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their lips.
Shear off your consecrated hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the barren heights, for the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his wrath.

versions.text: Cut off your hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the barren heights, for the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation of his wrath.
versions.explanation: נֵזֶר denotes hair that is long and dedicated/consecrated (as with a Nazirite vow), so "your hair" loses the note of shorn consecration that makes the mourning image so severe. The imperatives are feminine singular, addressed to Jerusalem personified as a woman, which "Shear off" preserves without over-explaining.

text: For the people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They have set their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, defiling it.
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire—something I never commanded and that never entered my mind.

So the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben Hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter; for they will bury in Topheth until there is no room left.
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with no one to drive them away.
And I will silence in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, for the land will lie in ruins.
